description: RISK R-B, STATED FIRST BECAUSE THE CLASS NAME INVERTS THE BEHAVIOUR: the prompt-mandated Java class for COTRN02C is transaction.TransactionViewController, but this program does not view - it ADDS, and this case is the add. Two independent sources say so: app/cbl/COTRN02C.cbl:5 'Function    : Add a new Transaction to TRANSACT file', and the transaction inventory row '| CT02 | COTRN02 | COTRN02C | Transaction Add |', which sits at README.md:224 in this checkout. This file's authoring brief cites README.md:222 for that row; the verified line is :224, and the number is corrected in the open rather than propagated, because a citation that does not resolve is worse than none (practices B1 and B4). Rule R1 governs the resolution - the name comes from the prompt, the behaviour comes from the source - so the class keeps its mandated name and nothing is renamed. The mirror image is parity/COTRN01C, whose program genuinely views. No case in this folder is downgraded to read-only to match the name: the EXEC CICS WRITE at :713 is pinned at its full 350 bytes by case19 and case20, and this case is the one whose final state proves a row actually landed. PROVENANCE - STATICALLY DERIVED AND NEVER CAPTURED (practice B12): every expected value below was derived by reading app/cbl/COTRN02C.cbl against the 350-byte layout of app/cpy/CVTRA05Y.cpy, the xxxI widths of app/cpy-bms/COTRN02.CPY and the real rows of app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt. None of it was captured from a live COBOL run, because none is possible in this environment: the Agent Action Plan records at section 0.7.6 that the only available COBOL compiler reports 'indexed file handler : disabled', and TRANSACT is an indexed KSDS that this program browses backwards, so the program's central operation cannot execute here at all. That is risk R-A, and substituting a derived baseline for a captured one is declared rather than absorbed. WHAT THIS CASE DRIVES: EIBCALEN is 218 and CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT arrives at '1', so NOT CDEMO-PGM-REENTER at :120 is false and :132 receives the map; EIBAID is DFHENTER, so the ordered EVALUATE at :133-152 takes its first arm at :134 and performs PROCESS-ENTER-KEY (the REENTER state, gate G38). Both validation paragraphs pass: the account half of VALIDATE-INPUT-KEY-FIELDS resolves through the CXACAIX alternate index and takes the DFHRESP(NORMAL) arm of READ-CXACAIX-FILE at :589-590, all eleven data fields are present, TTYPCD and TCATCD are numeric, TRNAMT satisfies the positional amount check, both dates are positionally valid and both CSUTLDTC calls at :393 and :413 report severity '0000' so the outer IFs at :397 and :417 accept outright, and MID is numeric. CONFIRMI holds 'Y', so the EVALUATE at :169 takes its first arm at :170-172 and performs ADD-TRANSACTION - the only arm of that EVALUATE that attempts an insert. THE IDENTIFIER GENERATOR: :444 moves HIGH-VALUES into TRAN-ID and :445-447 position a backward browse past the end of the file, read the record carrying the highest key, and end the browse. :448 moves that key into WS-TRAN-ID-N PIC 9(16) - an alphanumeric-to-numeric move out of TRAN-ID PIC X(16) - :449 adds one, and :451 renders it back into TRAN-ID as sixteen zero-padded digits. The seeded master's highest key is ...0003, so this run issues ...0004. The same three paragraphs serve a second caller: COPY-LAST-TRAN-DATA repeats the identical browse at :476-478 on the DFHPF5 arm, which is why neither paragraph may assume who called it. THE THREE STARTBR ARMS AND WHO OWNS THEM: STARTBR-TRANSACT-FILE at :642-668 issues EXEC CICS STARTBR DATASET(WS-TRANSACT-FILE) RIDFLD(TRAN-ID) KEYLENGTH(LENGTH OF TRAN-ID) RESP(WS-RESP-CD) RESP2(WS-REAS-CD), then evaluates WS-RESP-CD over three arms in source order with WHEN OTHER last (gate G30, rule R7). DFHRESP(NORMAL) at :653-654 is CONTINUE and is the arm this case and case20 take. DFHRESP(NOTFND) at :655-660 moves 'Y' to WS-ERR-FLG, moves 'Transaction ID NOT found...' to WS-MESSAGE, moves -1 to ACTIDINL and sends. WHEN OTHER at :661-667 displays the RESP and REAS pair and reports 'Unable to lookup Transaction...'. Neither rejecting arm is reachable from any parity case against this translation, and that is a deliberate documented property rather than a gap: TransactionRepository.startBrowse reports no status at all, so TransactionViewController.startbrTransactFile records NORMAL and calls startbrOutcome with OK unconditionally - the reasoning is set out on that method - and COTRN02CParityTest consumes forced outcomes only for the browse read, the write and the cross-reference read, never for startBrowse, while ParityHarness fails outright any run that declares a forced outcome nothing consumes. Both literals and both cursor placements are therefore asserted by the unit test that drives startbrOutcome directly, and this case takes the positioning arm the repository can actually report. Stating that boundary is practice B4; fabricating a forced outcome to counterfeit the arm would have failed the suite rather than proved anything. THE -1 TO ACTIDINL QUIRK, PRESERVED AND NEVER CORRECTED (practice B5): five error arms move -1 to ACTIDINL OF COTRN2AI - the two rejecting STARTBR arms at :659 and :666, the READPREV WHEN OTHER arm at :695, and both WRITE error arms at :740 and :747, the first of which covers DFHRESP(DUPKEY) and DFHRESP(DUPREC) together. Every one of those messages is about a transaction, yet the cursor goes to the Account ID field. That is not a defect to tidy: app/cpy-bms/COTRN02.CPY declares no transaction-identifier field at all - there is no TRNIDIN and no TRNID among its twenty-one payload fields - so the account field is the only place the program has to put the cursor, and a translation that redirected it somewhere more sensible would be changing behaviour. ACTIDINL is a COMP PIC S9(4) length item, which makes it validation metadata rather than data: it travels as this case's cursorField and never as a JSON payload member (gate G9). This case reaches it by the accepting route instead - :725 INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS puts the cursor back on the same field after a successful add. THE READPREV ENDFILE SIBLING: READPREV-TRANSACT-FILE at :673-697 likewise evaluates three arms with WHEN OTHER last. DFHRESP(NORMAL) at :686-687 continues with the record and its key in the record area, which is the arm this case takes. DFHRESP(ENDFILE) at :688-689 moves ZEROS to TRAN-ID and, crucially, raises no error flag - it is not an error but the empty-master path: with TRAN-ID zeroed, :448 yields nought, :449 adds one, and the first record ever written to an empty file carries TRAN-ID 0000000000000001. Getting that arm wrong is the difference between an empty master being loadable and being permanently unloadable. WHEN OTHER at :690-696 displays and rejects. case20 owns the ENDFILE arm, declaring TRANSACT with the empty shape - deliberately empty, and expressed as a declaration carrying its width and its copybook rather than as a tenth fixture, because app/data/ASCII holds exactly nine files and none of them is a transaction file. THE SHARED WHEN OTHER TEXT: STARTBR at :664 and READPREV at :693 move the same literal, 'Unable to lookup Transaction...', and each is preceded by DISPLAY 'RESP:' WS-RESP-CD 'REAS:' WS-REAS-CD at :662 and :691. Both operands are PIC S9(09) COMP VALUE ZEROS at :47-48, so each renders as nine characters and COBOL concatenates the four operands with no separator, giving lines of the form RESP:000000019REAS:000000000. That literal must never be crossed with the two cross-reference texts, which are different messages about different files: 'Unable to lookup Acct in XREF AIX file...' belongs to the CXACAIX path and is owned by case10, and 'Unable to lookup Card # in XREF file...' belongs to the CCXREF path and is owned by case14. This case emits no DISPLAY line at all, because only the WHEN OTHER arms produce one and this run reaches none of them. ENDBR HAS NO ERROR PATH: ENDBR-TRANSACT-FILE at :702-706 is a bare EXEC CICS ENDBR DATASET(WS-TRANSACT-FILE) with no RESP operand, no RESP2 operand and no EVALUATE after it. It has no outcome to drive and must never be given an error expectation in any case in this folder. Here both the READPREV at :446 and the ENDBR at :447 are genuinely reached, because the positioning at :445 succeeded and nothing raised the error flag; on any arm that does reject, SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN runs and its EXEC CICS RETURN at :530-534 ends the CICS task, so the remainder of ADD-TRANSACTION never executes at all. THE RECORD AND THE WRITE: :450 initializes TRAN-RECORD and :451-465 fill it, including a second FUNCTION NUMVAL-C conversion of TRNAMTI at :456-457 whose result is stored into TRAN-AMT PIC S9(09)V99 as the eleven-character zoned image 0000000123D, the trailing D carrying the positive overpunch for a final digit of 4 - so the stored value is +12.34, exactly the amount the re-edit at :383-386 had already put back on the screen in its +99999999.99 form by way of WS-TRAN-AMT-E. Numeric policy is scale exactly 2 with RoundingMode.DOWN through common.CobolDecimal, never double or float and never HALF_UP or HALF_EVEN, because the keyword ROUNDED appears zero times across all twenty-eight COBOL programs (rules R2, R3 and R4; gates G23 and G24). The record written at :713 is the full 350 bytes CVTRA05Y declares - 16+2+4+10+100+11+9+50+50+10+16+26+26+20 - with the trailing FILLER PIC X(20) present and space filled (gates G19 and G21); dropping FILLER would shorten the record and move every offset behind it. The write reports NORMAL, so :725 performs INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS, which blanks every input receiver and is why every field on the sent screen is empty; :726 blanks WS-MESSAGE; :727 moves DFHGREEN into ERRMSGC, the program's only attribute move anywhere; and :728-733 STRING two literals, TRAN-ID DELIMITED BY SPACE and a full stop into WS-MESSAGE. Both literals carry a space at the joining edge, so the notice holds two spaces after 'successfully.', and a zero-filled sixteen-digit key contains no space, so DELIMITED BY SPACE copies all sixteen digits. :520 then moves WS-MESSAGE PIC X(80) into ERRMSGO PIC X(78), losing the last two bytes, left-justified and space-padded, per rule R5. TRANSACT is left holding four rows in key sequence. THE INPUTS, BY BINDING KEY ONLY (gate G46): each dataset is named by its application.yml binding key rather than by name, so not one fully-qualified mainframe dataset name appears anywhere in this file. CCXREF is seeded from cardxref.txt exactly as shipped, at 36 bytes per row, where CVACT03Y declares 50 as 16+9+11+14; the 36-to-50 pad of the trailing FILLER PIC X(14) is declared as a normalisation and applied once by ParityCase.DatasetNormalisation.normaliseSeedRow, which is its sole owner, so this case does not pre-pad a single row (gate G16, risk R-F). There is no separate CXACAIX seed, because CXACAIX is a PATH over the CCXREF base cluster: one seeded cluster answers both access paths as an alternate-index finder rather than as a second table (gate G45). ACCTDAT is seeded from acctdata.txt precisely to make visible what practice B5 requires be preserved - WS-ACCTDAT-FILE is declared at :40 and appears in no DATASET operand anywhere in the program, and COPY CVACT01Y at :89 is a dead include, so the file is opened by nothing and read by nothing. It is therefore seeded and never touched, and no ACCTDAT entry appears in expectedWrites or expectedFinalState in this case or in any other case in this folder. TRANSACT itself is declared inline as three rows of 350 bytes, so no tenth fixture is requested. NO REWRITE AND NO DELETE: TRANSACT is only ever browsed, read and written. No program in this codebase issues EXEC CICS REWRITE or EXEC CICS DELETE against it, so TransactionRepository deliberately declares neither operation - a repository offering them would be offering an access path the COBOL never had, and no case here can assert one. STATELESSNESS, THE CLOCK AND THE COMMAREA: all conversation state travels in the payload and none in a session (rule R6, gate G37) - the commarea arrives as a request member and leaves as the navigation map. It is the 160 bytes of COCOM01Y plus the separate 58-byte CDEMO-CT02-INFO extension declared at :72-80 as 16+16+8+1+1+16, which stays its own field and is never folded into NavigationContext, giving the 218 bytes EIBCALEN reports (practice B11). The clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:34 and both date inputs are the fixed literal 2022-07-18, never a computed today and never a captured timestamp (practice B7); the pinned instant is the program's own version footer, 'Ver: CardDemo_v1.0-15-g27d6c6f-68 Date: 2022-07-19 23:12:34 CDT', which is why POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :552-571 yields CURDATEO 07/19/22 and CURTIMEO 23:12:34 beside TRNNAMEO CT02, PGMNAMEO COTRN02C and the two COTTL01Y titles at PIC X(40). The charset is named explicitly as US-ASCII rather than left to a platform default (practice B8). expectedReturnCode is 0 and jobParameters is empty: COTRN02C contains no CALL 'CEE3ABD' anywhere, so no path here abends and gate G35 does not apply. The response returns to the same transaction with RETURN_TRANSID and names COTRN02C, COTRN02 and COTRN2A as the echo of CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM; there is no EXEC CICS XCTL to another program on this path, so gate G40 does not apply either. GOVERNING PRACTICES: review_rules returns exactly one line, 'No user rules provided.', and that line is the whole document - confirmed directly while authoring this case. No user rule governs this file, and their absence is not licence to lower the bar: the enterprise practices of Agent Action Plan section 0.10.2 bind instead, and the ones this case turns on are B1, B3, B4, B5, B7, B8, B11 and B12, cited by name throughout and never reproduced. The reference trees under app/cbl, app/cpy, app/cpy-bms and app/data are read-only and were read, never written (practice B3). Gates this case carries: G15, G16, G18, G19, G21, G23, G24, G30, G37, G38, G45, G46, G47 and G51 - the unit is built as a plain object through its constructor and its MAIN-PARA method is called directly, with no MockMvc, no TestRestTemplate, no servlet container and no JobLauncher between the assertion and the decision. Gate G32 does not apply because this program contains no GO TO at all, and G39 and G43 do not apply because this screen paginates nothing and has no 9300-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC.
